title: Midwife lead care
description: Understand what to expect during midwife and doctor visits.

contentSections.title: Your LMC
contentSections.content:
Your LMC holds the legal, professional, and practical responsibility for ensuring both you and your pēpi (baby) receive the right maternity care. This role may be filled by a self-employed midwife, a hospital midwife, or a private obstetrician.

  • Self-employed midwives provide care throughout your pregnancy, labour, birth, and the time you spend at home with your pēpi.
  • Hospital midwives work as part of a team, supporting you during pregnancy, birth, and at home after your pēpi arrives.
  • Private obstetricians oversee your care during pregnancy, labour, and birth, and collaborate with self-employed midwives for postnatal support at home. Their services involve an additional fee.

contentSections.title: How to find a LMC?
contentSections.content:
For help finding a midwife you can visit:
  • Maternity Services
  • Find your midwife

contentSections.title: What to expect during your visits?
contentSections.content:
Your LMC is available 24/7 to support you throughout pregnancy, labour, and after birth. They will:

  • During pregnancy: Create a care plan for labour and birth, and monitor your overall health (including any medical or mental health conditions). They can also carry out regular antenatal checks such as blood pressure, urine, weight, and pēpi's heartbeat. If you are healthy, these checks usually happen monthly until 32 weeks, every two weeks until 36 weeks, and weekly until birth. More frequent visits are arranged if needed.
  • For your health: Provide advice on staying well, help with social challenges like family violence, unplanned pregnancy, work or financial stress. They can refer you or your pēpi to specialists when required.
  • For your pēpi: Explain screening options for Down Syndrome and other conditions. They can prescribe important supplements (e.g., folic acid and iodine), and support with antenatal and newborn screening.
  • After birth: The LMC visit you in hospital and at home at least seven times in the weeks following birth. They can also refer you to your chosen Well Child Tamariki Ora provider (with care usually handed over when your pēpi is about five weeks old), and help you enrol your pēpi at a general practice for doctor and nurse services.
